findings.summary: White count numerals sit on the agreeing green (#1baf7a, 2.81:1) and the unplaced grey (#9a9892, 2.86:1) segments, just under the 3:1 floor for large text. The counts are legible but marginal, and a reader with reduced contrast sensitivity will lose them first; a darker fill or a dark numeral would settle it. Cause: scripts/figures_jt60sa_mapping_study.py:101.

The live projection's long strings are hard-wrapped at a fixed character count, so words break across lines with a space inserted ('i n tesla', 'provi ding', 'equ il ibrium'). A reader must reassemble the description by eye, and the introduced space can read as content. Wrapping on word boundaries, or truncating with an ellipsis, would keep the prose intact. Cause: scripts/figures_discovery_to_mapping.py:450.

The provenance line under the panel title prints a machine-local absolute path (/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-codex/tests/fixtures/mapping_handoff_example.json). In a published report it names a directory no reader can resolve and exposes a home path; the repository-relative path or the document's own identity would carry the same provenance. Cause: scripts/figures_discovery_to_mapping.py:470.

The wrapped 'Non-Conformance Reports' title pushes the NCR card's code line down one line, so it sits at y=336 while the other four first-row codes sit at y=300 and the row reads ragged. Nothing overlaps or clips; a fixed subtitle baseline, or reserving two title lines for every card, would align them. Cause: scripts/figures_icp_knowledge_map.py:1148.

method: Each attached PNG was opened and read as a rendered image; readings were then confirmed or corrected by measuring the PNG itself (ink extents against the canvas edge, text-row and glyph-class profiles, and WCAG contrast of sampled colours). All 150 frames of each GIF were scanned for ink outside the canvas. No SVG was opened.
